The County page gives no area; it mentions Toulouse, Quercy, Rouergue, Albi, Nîmes, Provence, Gothia (Septimania), the Duchy of Narbonne and Auvergne without dating any extent, and the infobox says 'Established: 778, by Charlemagne'. 52,887 km2 (bbox to 4.7 E, 42.5-44.9 N): the 1040 outline plus Cliopatria's County of Rouergue shape (27.9k km2, which reaches the Rhône, far beyond the 9,007 km2 of Rouergue proper on the Rouergue page). Raymond IV is styled 'count of Toulouse and Rouergue, margrave of Provence' in a bull of 22 July 1096 and William IV is 'Count of Toulouse, Margrave of Provence, and Duke of Narbonne from 1061 to 1094' (his page), so the union is page-supported by 1096 and the titles by 1061; the year 1066 is Cliopatria's (ledger confidence 1).
52,840 km2, the 1066 outline: no page opened dates a change in 1147. The County page notes only the 1152 act naming the count 'count of Toulouse, duke of Narbonne, and marquis of Provence'.
52,887 km2, the 1066 outline again; Henry II and Eleanor's attempt on Toulouse (1159, Eleanor page) took no ground.
52,816 km2, outline noise; the County page dates only a ten-year quarrel between the town council and Raymond V ending 1189 (submission), no border move.
52,840 km2, the 1066 outline. Shape runs to 1209: the crusade takes Béziers (22 July 1209) and Carcassonne (15 August 1209), so the Cliopatria change in 1210 is a year after the ledger loss.

Holds in Cliopatria to 1215; at the Fourth Lateran Council (November 1215) Raymond VI's conquered lands go to Simon and the rest is put under Church protection, so Cliopatria's empty years 1216-1219 are explained.

region.text: the county as Cliopatria draws it in 990: Cliopatria's 990 outline (bbox 0.6-2.5 E, 42.5-44.8 N); the page mentions Toulouse, Quercy, Rouergue, Albi, Nîmes and Gothia without dating an extent

ledger.note: 990: the County of Toulouse, established by Charlemagne in 778 according to the page's infobox, is drawn from Cliopatria's first shape. No page opened gives the county's extent in 990.

Page silent on 1066: Cliopatria adds its County of Rouergue shape (27.9k km2, reaching the Rhône) to Toulouse in 1066. The latest page-dated sign of the union is the bull of 22 July 1096 styling Raymond IV 'count of Toulouse and Rouergue, margrave of Provence'; William IV is 'Duke of Narbonne' from 1061 (his page).

region.text: the area encompassing Carcassonne, Albi, and Béziers

ledger.note: 1209: the Albigensian Crusade takes Béziers (22 July) and Carcassonne (15 August); in autumn 'Simon de Montfort is granted control of the area encompassing Carcassonne, Albi, and Béziers'. The lands were Raymond Roger Trencavel's, drawn inside Toulouse by Cliopatria until 1209.

region.text: the county of Raymond VI as it stood in 1215, given to Simon de Montfort (conquered lands) and to the Church's protection (the rest)

ledger.note: 1215: at the Fourth Lateran Council Simon de Montfort is proclaimed Count of Toulouse (the County of Toulouse page: 'made official in November 1215'): 'Lands of Raymond VI conquered by the crusade go to Simon, and unconquered lands are placed under Church protection until Raymond VII comes of age.' Cliopatria draws nothing for the county in 1216-1219, so the whole 1210-1215 outline is treated as lost; the split between conquered and church-protected land is not on the page.

1217: Raymond VI retakes Toulouse. 'On 12 September 1217 Raymond VI retakes Toulouse without a fight while Montfort is in the Foix region.' Montfort was killed at the siege of Toulouse in 1218 (County page).
1222: Raymond VII recovers the county. 'Raymond VII has reclaimed all the lands lost, following the death of Raymond VI that year.' The region is the 1215 outline, the page naming no places.
1224: Carcassonne and the Trencavel lands return. 'Amaury de Montfort abandons Carcassonne, and Raymond VII returns to reclaim the area. Amaury cedes his remaining lands to Louis VIII.'

region.text: Béziers, Carcassonne and Beaucaire, retaken by the crown

ledger.note: 1226: Louis VIII's crusade takes the Languedoc coast. 'Béziers, Carcassonne, Beaucaire, and Marseille are retaken without resistance'; Avignon surrenders in early September and is occupied on 9 September. The zone is the three Languedoc departments of those towns; Marseille and Avignon (Provence) lie outside Cliopatria's county.

region.text: the eastern provinces of Raymond's lands

ledger.note: 1229: the Treaty of Paris, signed at Meaux on 12 April 1229, ends the war. Raymond VII is recognised as count of Toulouse and swears allegiance to Louis IX; his daughter Joan is to marry Louis's brother Alphonse of Poitiers, and the county reverts to the crown if they have no heir. The Raymond VII page gives January 1229 for the signing.

region.text: the eastern provinces: the Languedoc coast with Béziers, Carcassonne and Beaucaire

ledger.note: 1229: Raymond VII 'ceded more than half his land to the French crown' and gave up 'the eastern provinces of his lands' (Treaty page); the Raymond VII page adds that he 'ceded the former Trencavel viscounty to Louis IX'. The Papacy also gained the Comtat Venaissin (outside Cliopatria's county).

1242: after the Saintonge War Raymond VII is 'forced to surrender Saverdun and Bram' to Louis IX. The page gives no separate date for the surrender; 1242 is the year of the alliance and war (confidence lowered from 3 to 2 by the eu-10-c reviewer).

1249: Raymond VII dies at Toulouse on 27 September without a male heir; 'Alphonse became count of Toulouse' with Joan, and the county passes from the house of Saint-Gilles to the Capetian count of Poitiers: same state and colour. Cliopatria ends its row here.

region.text: the county of Toulouse as Alphonse held it

ledger.note: 1271: Alphonse of Poitiers dies at Savona on 21 August 1271 'without heirs' and the county passes to the French crown. The County page: 'Acquired by France: 1271'; Parlement ruled in 1283 that Toulouse should revert to the crown without male heirs.

wars.name: Albigensian Crusade
wars.outcome: The crusade took the Trencavel lands (1209), made Simon de Montfort count of Toulouse (1215), lost them again to Raymond VI and VII (1217-1224), and ended with Louis VIII's campaign of 1226 and the Treaty of Paris of 12 April 1229.
wars.note: Raymond VII's page gives January 1229 for the treaty; the Treaty page and the Crusade page give 12 April 1229.

wars.name: Siege of Toulouse (1159)
wars.outcome: 'In 1159, Eleanor and Henry unsuccessfully tried to enforce her claim to Toulouse through her grandmother'; no ground changed hands.
wars.note: Listed to show it was considered; the claim passed through Philippa, daughter of William IV, who married William IX of Aquitaine (William IV page), and was pursued 'off and on, for years'.

wars.name: Saintonge War
wars.outcome: Raymond VII allied with Hugh of La Marche and Henry III of England against Louis IX in 1242 and was 'forced to surrender Saverdun and Bram'.
wars.note: The page dates the alliance to 1242 and says nothing of the peace; the Treaty of Lorris of 1243 is not on any page opened.

certainty.note: Feudal frontiers drawn from regions; the Treaty of Paris of 1229 cedes the 'eastern provinces' without a boundary on any page opened.

notes:
Start: the County page's infobox says 'Established: 778, by Charlemagne', preceded by the Gothic March; the dossier is drawn from 990 because Cliopatria's first shape begins then and no page opened gives the county's extent for 778-989 (Cliopatria's Aquitaine row, 629-895, covers the area earlier). The found caption says so.
End: Cliopatria ends the county in 1249 but the County page and Alphonse's page keep it one unit under Alphonse of Poitiers and Joan until 1271; the dossier ends 1271 with a new keyframe 1250-1271. Page budget: the County article is thin on land (no area, no 1066), so eight pages were opened (budget five); the Rouergue pages are shared with the county-of-rouergue dossier.
Cliopatria problems: (1) the 1220-1226 shape of 1,105 km2 contradicts 'Raymond VII has reclaimed all the lands lost' (1222); (2) there is no shape for 1216-1219 and 1227-1235; (3) the 1236-1249 shape of 48,206 km2 still reaches the Rhône although the Treaty page says Raymond ceded more than half his land and the eastern provinces; (4) the 'County of Rouergue' row (27.9k km2 to the Rhône) is not Rouergue (9,007 km2) but the Toulouse family's eastern holdings (Gothia, Narbonne titles): see the county-of-rouergue notes.
Not modelled for lack of a page: the Marquisate of Provence and Duchy of Narbonne as territory (titles only, 1061/1094/1152); the 1243 Treaty of Lorris; the Agenais, Quercy and Albigeois as separate pieces; the extent of 'conquered' versus 'church-protected' land in 1215; the War of Philippa's claim (undated: 'fought, off and on, for years', William IV page). Vassalage: Cliopatria lists the county as a member of (Kingdom of France) throughout; Raymond VII swore allegiance to Louis IX in 1229 (Treaty page): the vassal_start for Toulouse belongs in the kingdom-of-france dossier.
Counterpart without a dossier: 'Simon de Montfort (crusader lordship)' (suggested slug montfort-crusader-lordship) (Simon de Montfort's domain, 1209-1224; Carcassonne, Albi, Béziers; Count of Toulouse from November 1215). Gazetteer names needed: Saverdun, Bram (places).
Rulers omitted: no complete list opened (William IV 1061-1094, Raymond IV 1094-1105, Raymond VII 1222-1249, Alphonse and Joan 1249-1271 are on the pages opened).
